title: Cell Hashing Protocol
author: Brenton Paolella
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yp6fvre

Carefully remove and discard the ethanol wash.

steps.title: Prepare single‑cell suspensions
steps.instruction: Obtain all single‑cell suspensions from each sample/condition that will be multiplexed, keep each in a separate tube on ice, and if a single sample will be super‑loaded divide it into equal aliquots before staining with distinct hashing antibodies.

steps.title: Count cells and assess viability
steps.instruction: Count cells in each tube, record total cell number and viability (>95 %) in a cell‑count table, and include dead cells in the total count; if many dead cells are present, perform live‑cell enrichment (e.g., FACS) before proceeding.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in staining buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cells in 100 µL staining buffer (2 % BSA, 0.02 % Tween‑20 in PBS). This volume is suitable for ~200 000–1 000 000 cells per tube.

steps.title: Block Fc receptors
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL Fc‑blocking reagent (FcX, BioLegend) to each tube and incubate 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Add hashing antibody
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL (1 µg) of the single‑cell hashing antibody to each tube and incubate 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash stained cells
steps.instruction: Perform three washes with 1 mL staining buffer (2 % BSA/0.02 % Tween in PBS): add 1 mL, spin 5 min at 400 g at 4 °C, discard supernatant; repeat two more times.

steps.title: Resuspend in capture buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in cell‑capture buffer at the concentration required for the downstream platform (e.g., ~200 µL if ~300 000 cells remain). Approximate target concentrations: 10x Genomics ~ 500 cells/µL, Drop‑seq ~ 200 cells/µL, super‑loading ~ 1 500 cells/µL or higher.

steps.title: Filter cell suspension
steps.instruction: Pass the cell suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer (e.g., Flowmi) to remove aggregates.

steps.title: Verify concentration after filtration
steps.instruction: Count the filtered cells on a Countess instrument, record the concentration in the cell‑count table, and keep the suspension on ice.

steps.title: Pool samples
steps.instruction: Pool all samples/conditions at the desired proportions and proceed immediately to the single‑cell capture step.

steps.title: Run single‑cell capture
steps.instruction: Perform Drop‑seq (Macosko et al., 2015) or 10x Genomics 3′ v2 assay exactly as described in the manufacturer’s protocol, stopping just before cDNA amplification.

steps.title: Add HTO additive primer
steps.instruction: Add the HTO PCR additive primer (2 µM) to the cDNA PCR: 1 µL for 10x Genomics or 0.4 µL for Drop‑seq; subtract this volume from the water component of the PCR mix.

steps.title: Separate hashtags with 0.6× SPRI
steps.instruction: Add 0.6× SPRI beads to the cDNA reaction as described in the 10x or Drop‑seq protocol, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on a magnetic rack until the solution clears, then keep the supernatant (contains hashtags) and retain the beads (contain full‑length mRNA cDNA).

steps.title: First hashtag SPRI purification
steps.instruction: Purify the hashtag‑containing supernatant with a 2× SPRI cleanup: add 1.4× SPRI beads to achieve a final 2× volume (e.g., 100 µL supernatant + 300 µL beads), transfer to a low‑bind 1.5 mL tube, incubate 10 min at RT, magnet for ~2 min, wash once with 450 µL 80 % ethanol (stand 30 s), briefly centrifuge, then resuspend beads in 50 µL water.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.4× SPRI beads (e.g., 300 µL to 100 µL supernatant).

steps.title: Second hashtag SPRI purification
steps.instruction: Perform a second 2× SPRI cleanup: add 100 µL SPRI reagent directly to the resuspended beads, mix, incubate 10 min at RT, magnet ~2 min, wash twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (each stand 30 s), briefly centrifuge, discard ethanol, air‑dry beads 2 min (do not overdry), resuspend in 15 µL water, mix vigorously and incubate 5 min at RT, then place on magnet and transfer the clear supernatant to PCR tubes.

substeps.instruction: Mix and incubate 10 min at RT.
Vigorously pipette mix, incubate 5 min at RT.
Place on magnet, transfer supernatant to PCR tubes.

steps.title: Set up hashtag PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare a 50 µL PCR reaction containing ~1 µL purified hashtag fraction, 45 µL 2× KAPA HiFi PCR Master Mix, 2.5 µL TruSeq DNA D7xx_s primer (10 µM i7 index), and 2.5 µL P5 oligo (10 µM) (or P5‑SMART‑PCR hybrid oligo for Drop‑seq). Adjust water volume so the total is 50 µL.

steps.title: Purify hashtag PCR product
steps.instruction: Clean the PCR product with a 2× SPRI cleanup: add 100 µL SPRI reagent, incubate 5 min at RT, magnet 1 min, wash twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (each stand 30 s), briefly centrifuge, discard ethanol, air‑dry beads 2 min, resuspend in 15 µL water, mix vigorously, incubate 5 min at RT, place on magnet and transfer the clear supernatant to a new PCR tube.

substeps.instruction: Vigorously mix, incubate 5 min at RT.
Place on magnet, transfer supernatant to PCR tube.

steps.title: Quality‑control hashtag library
steps.instruction: Run the purified library on a BioAnalyzer, Qubit or qPCR; a ~90 bp peak indicates primer only, while a dominant ~180 bp peak corresponds to correctly sized hashtags; larger fragments (>186 bp) suggest over‑amplification.

steps.title: Prepare antibody pool during Fc block
steps.instruction: While cells are incubating with Fc block, make an antibody pool containing 1 µg (or titrated amount) of each TotalSeq™ antibody plus 1 µg of the single‑cell hashing antibody; centrifuge the pool at 14 000 × g, 2–8 °C for 10 min, carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, and add the clarified antibody cocktail to the cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Combine 1 µg each TotalSeq antibody and 1 µg hashing antibody.

steps.title: Count pooled cell suspension
steps.instruction: Count the final pooled cell suspension; for 10x super‑loading aim for ~1 500 cells/µL (≈1.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL) and record the count in the cell‑count table.

steps.title: Quantify DNA and transfer
steps.instruction: Quantify the final library using Qubit or NanoDrop (acceptable though less sensitive), then transfer the appropriate volume to PCR strip tubes for downstream sequencing.
